# Hazard

## Realistic data

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
using CEVE543Utils, CSV, DataFrames, Distributions
using CairoMakie, LaTeXStrings, Random, Printf, Statistics
set_theme!(theme_minimal(); fontsize=20)
colors = Makie.wong_colors()
```

```{julia}
#| output: false
rng = MersenneTwister(824)
annmax = CSV.read("8638610-annmax.csv", DataFrame)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(760, 250))
ax = Axis(
    fig[1, 1];
    title="Sewells Point, Norfolk",
    xlabel="Year",
    ylabel="Annual Maximum Water Level",
)
scatter!(ax, annmax.year, annmax.lsl)
fig
```

## Fitting

We fit a Generalized Extreme Value distribution (more on that soon!)

```{julia}
gev = only(getdistribution(gevfit(annmax.lsl)))
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(760, 350))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel="annual maximum water level (ft)", ylabel="density")
hist!(ax, annmax.lsl; bins=20, normalization=:pdf, color=(:gray, 0.5))
lines!(ax, range(3, 9; length=400), pdf.(gev, range(3, 9; length=400)); linewidth=3)
fig
```

## Return Levels

```{julia}
#| output: false
n_obs = nrow(annmax)
lsl = sort(annmax.lsl; rev=true)
p_obs = (1:n_obs) ./ (n_obs + 1)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(760, 330))
ax = Axis(
    fig[1, 1];
    xscale=log10,
    xlabel=L"\text{return period } T \text{ (years)}",
    ylabel=L"\text{annual maximum water level (ft)}",
    xticks=([1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 100, 1000], string.([1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 100, 1000])),
)
Ts = 10 .^ range(0.05, 3; length=300)
lines!(
    ax,
    Ts,
    quantile.(gev, 1 .- 1 ./ Ts);
    linewidth=3,
    color=colors[1],
    label=L"\text{fitted GEV}",
)
scatter!(ax, 1 ./ p_obs, lsl; color=colors[2], label=L"\text{observations}")
axislegend(ax; position=:lt)
fig
```

# Risk

## Illustrative damage function

Let $h$ be the water level at the gauge, in feet.
A building sits 5.5 ft above the gauge.
Assume total loss at 8.5 ft; between those two the curve is convex.

```{julia}
#| output: false
damage(h) = clamp((h - 5.5) / 3, 0, 1)^1.5
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(760, 260))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel=L"\text{water level (ft)}", ylabel=L"\text{damage (fraction)}")
xs = range(3, 9; length=400)
lines!(ax, xs, damage.(xs); linewidth=3, color=:firebrick)
fig
```

## Expected damage with $n = 10$

```{julia}
levels = rand(rng, gev, 10)

println("level   ", round.(levels; digits=2))
println("damage  ", round.(damage.(levels); digits=2))
@printf("average %.3g", mean(damage.(levels)))
```

## The estimator

$\hat\theta_n = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} g(X_i)$, with $X$ the water level and $g$ the damage function, estimates $\theta = E[g(X)]$:

1. Draw $n$ years.
1. Apply $g$ to each.
1. Average.

```{julia}
#| output: false
function expected_damage(dist, n)
    levels = rand(rng, dist, n)
    return mean(damage.(levels))
end
```

## $\hat\theta_n$: a random variable with $\mathrm{SE} = \mathrm{sd}(g(X))/\sqrt{n}$


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
draws = rand(rng, gev, 1_000_000)
```

```{julia}
#| output: false
sd_g = std(damage.(draws))
sample_sizes = (100, 10_000)
estimates = [[expected_damage(gev, n) for _ in 1:10_000] for n in sample_sizes]
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(900, 300))
for (col, n) in enumerate(sample_sizes)
    ests = estimates[col]
    se = sd_g / sqrt(n)
    ax = Axis(fig[1, col]; title="n = $n", xlabel=L"\hat\theta_n")
    hideydecorations!(ax)
    hist!(ax, ests; bins=60, normalization=:pdf, color=(colors[2], 0.7))
    vlines!(ax, [mean(ests)]; color=colors[1], linewidth=3)
    vlines!(ax, mean(ests) .+ [-1, 1] .* se; color=colors[1], linewidth=2, linestyle=:dash)
end
fig
```

## How many years do we need to simulate?

From the whiteboard, we know we need $n = (\mathrm{CV}/\varepsilon)^2$ simulations, where $\varepsilon$ is one standard error expressed as a fraction of the answer.

```{julia}
#| output: false
cv(v) = std(v) / mean(v)
n_years(c, ε) = ceil(Int, (c / ε)^2)
```

## Comparing simulations

How many draws do we need to estimate damage versus hazard with $\varepsilon = 0.01$?

```{julia}
ε = 0.01
cv_damage = cv(damage.(draws))
cv_hazard = cv(draws)

@printf("damage  CV %.3g, n %d\n", cv_damage, n_years(cv_damage, ε))
@printf("hazard  CV %.3g, n %d\n", cv_hazard, n_years(cv_hazard, ε))
```

## The exceedance probability curve

Sort the simulated damages from largest to smallest.
Rank $i$ gets $\hat p_i = i/(n+1)$ and $\hat T_i = 1/\hat p_i$ per Weibull plotting positions.

```{julia}
#| output: false
n_sim = 10_000
losses = sort(damage.(rand(rng, gev, n_sim)); rev=true)
p_sim = (1:n_sim) ./ (n_sim + 1)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
fig = Figure(; size=(760, 280))
ax = Axis(
    fig[1, 1];
    xscale=log10,
    xlabel=L"\text{return period } T \text{ (years)}",
    ylabel=L"\text{damage (fraction of value)}",
    xticks=([1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 100, 1000], string.([1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 100, 1000])),
)
lines!(ax, 1 ./ p_sim, losses; linewidth=3, color=:firebrick)
fig
```

## If we know $F$, we can use smarter sampling

Write $F$ for the cumulative distribution function of the water level and $f$ for its density.
Substituting $u = F(x)$ turns the integral into an average over quantiles, which we evaluate on a uniform grid of $u$.

$$
\theta = \int d(x) f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^1 d(F^{-1}(u))\,\mathrm{d}u
$$

## The two compared at two sample sizes

```{julia}
function run_mc_comparison(n)
    u = (0.5:1.0:n) ./ n
    theta_grid = mean(damage.(quantile.(gev, u)))

    @printf(
        "n = %6d  Monte Carlo %.4g  quantiles %.4g\n",
        n,
        expected_damage(gev, n),
        theta_grid
    )
end
run_mc_comparison(1_000)
run_mc_comparison(10_000)
```
